title: Sample: A pricing refactor that quietly breaks its callers

findings.title: 2 call site(s) incompatible with new signature of `format_price`
findings.description: `format_price` changed (parameter `currency` removed; required parameter `locale` added). 2 of 3 call site(s) in the repository no longer match the new signature.
findings.failure_scenario: src/billing/invoice.py:9 still calls `format_price` the old way: it passes unexpected keyword argument `currency`. Python raises TypeError when that line runs.

suggested_test.description: Update the incompatible callers, then add a regression test that calls `format_price` the way those callers do.
suggested_test.code:
from billing.pricing import format_price


def test_format_price_matches_callers():
    # mirror the argument shape used at the call sites listed in the evidence
    result = format_price(amount=..., locale=...)
    assert result == ...  # expected value for these inputs

explanation.text: A caller still uses the old calling convention. In Python this raises TypeError at call time; in TypeScript it fails compilation.

ai_analysis.explanation: The new signature of `format_price` changes the required parameter from `currency` to `locale`, making it incompatible with existing call sites.
ai_analysis.failure_scenario: A function calls `format_price` with a `currency` argument, but the function is expecting a `locale` argument. This will cause a TypeError when trying to execute the function.

suggested_test.description: Test that calling `format_price` with a `currency` argument raises a TypeError.

findings.title: Condition logic changed: `>` → `>=`
findings.description: Line 11 in `apply_discount` changed only in `>` → `>=`; the condition's boundary or polarity is different now.
findings.failure_scenario: Inputs exactly at the boundary (or on the side the condition now excludes/includes) take the other branch than before — the classic off-by-one / inverted-condition regression.

suggested_test.description: Add boundary-value tests: the threshold itself, one below, and one above, asserting the intended branch for each.

explanation.text: A comparison/boolean operator or negation changed. Boundary behaviour differs, which is a classic source of off-by-one and inverted-condition bugs.

ai.overall_assessment: The riskiest aspect of this change is the potential for incorrect calculations due to the changed condition logic in `format_price`. This could lead to inaccurate invoices being generated, resulting in financial losses. The new signature of `format_price` also introduces a new source of errors if not handled properly.

limitations: Static, name-based reference resolution: dynamic dispatch, reflection, monkey-patching, and dependency injection are not followed.
